req.title: Index renders even with zero posts
req.statement: The system shall render the index page with 'No posts' or empty state when the post table is empty.
triggers: index renders even with zero posts

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-037 requires the index page (GET /) to render successfully with HTTP 2xx even when the post table is empty. The pre-loaded fixture contains 1 post, so tests must explicitly clear the post table to create the zero-posts state. Three test cases are designed: (1) positive — empty post table yields HTTP 200 and a valid HTML response body; (2) negative — verifying that a bad HTTP method (POST) to / yields 405, confirming the route is GET-only; (3) boundary — the transition from 1 post to 0 posts (deleting the only row) still yields HTTP 200, catching off-by-one mutations in the post-count branch. All tests use exact status code assertions and inspect response body content to maximise mutation kill rate.

tests.name: test_index_empty_posts_returns_200
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
All rows deleted from post table so it is empty

expected: Response body is non-empty bytes (HTML rendered)
trace: R-FLASKR-037: index renders even with zero posts -> HTTP 2xx response
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db, get_db

def test_index_empty_posts_returns_200():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
        db = get_db()
        db.execute('DELETE FROM post')
        db.commit()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert len(r.data) > 0
    assert b'html' in r.data.lower() or b'<' in r.data
    os.unlink(path)

test_index_empty_posts_returns_200()

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_index_post_method_not_allowed():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/')
    assert r.status_code == 405
    assert r.status_code != 200
    assert r.status_code != 404
    os.unlink(path)

test_index_post_method_not_allowed()

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db, get_db

def test_index_after_deleting_last_post_returns_200():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
        db = get_db()
        # Insert a user and a post to simulate the pre-loaded fixture
        from werkzeug.security import generate_password_hash
        db.execute(
            'INSERT INTO user (username, password) VALUES (?, ?)',
            ('testuser', generate_password_hash('testpass'))
        )
        db.execute(
            "INSERT INTO post (title, body, author_id) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
            ('only post', 'body text', 1)
        )
        db.commit()
        count_before = db.execute('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM post').fetchone()[0]
        assert count_before == 1
        db.execute('DELETE FROM post WHERE id = 1')
        db.commit()
        count_after = db.execute('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM post').fetchone()[0]
        assert count_after == 0
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert r.status_code != 500
    assert len(r.data) > 0
    os.unlink(path)

test_index_after_deleting_last_post_returns_200()
